chunks: Describing your ECAD experience. The question: What experience do you have with ECAD software?
The interviewer wants to know how far you have taken a real board in design software, and whether you can explain the choices you made.
Name one project, describe a few decisions with reasons, say how you checked your work, and mention one mistake and what you changed afterward.
Think of giving a guided tour of one house you built. You say why the walls are where they are, how you checked that they stand, and which door you had to rehang.
A good answer in miniature is that tour: one board, three decisions, one check, one mistake.
Each rung builds on the one below. A strong intern answer usually owns rungs 1 to 5 on at least one board and has an opinion about 6.
Don't skip to the top: "constraint-driven DDR layout" without the lower rungs sounds hollow.
Footprint: the pattern of copper pads that a part is soldered onto. Stackup: the order and thickness of the copper and insulating layers inside the board.
Net class: a group of connections that share rules, such as how wide their copper paths (traces) must be.
DRC (design rule check): an automatic check of the layout against the factory's limits. BOM (bill of materials): the list of parts to buy, with part numbers.
Here is a skeleton with placeholders. "My project was [board and purpose] in [tool] . I made the footprints from datasheets and checked them against a 1:1 printout.
I chose a [number] -layer stackup because [reason, such as a ground layer under the signals] . I made the power traces wider, sized from the current they carry.
I ran the design rule check with the factory's limits, looked at the output files in a separate viewer, and had a classmate review the schematic.
When I first powered the board, [a real mistake] showed up, so I [fixed the board and the library] ."
Replace every bracket with something true, and delete any step you did not do. That is the whole idea.

"I've done [N] boards in [tool] , including [project] , end to end: libraries from datasheets, schematic with ERC, a four-layer stackup, net classes with trace widths sized from current, USB as a 90-ohm differential pair, DRC with the fab's rules, and Gerber, drill, BOM and pick-and-place.
At bring-up I found a footprint error, fixed the board with a bodge, and then fixed the library. I'm weaker on DDR and RF and want to learn them."
Quick check. Which statement best describes a footprint?
